President Donald Trump responded to Elon Musk distancing himself from his movement on Thursday after the billionaire publicly declared he was “not MAGA” in his appearance at The New York Times’ DealBook Summit.

“What can I tell you? I mean, you have to ask — there are lots of definitions out there. MAGA, to me, means something very specific, and when people veer from it, they don’t do very well.”

He added, “But Elon is — Elon’s got very good intentions. I mean, he was with me the whole — he traveled with me.”

Musk made the MAGA-free reboot in a video call from China, where he joined Trump as part of his delegation on his trip to meet with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China, per NBC News.

The billionaire — in his comments to The Times’ Andrew Ross Sorkin — acknowledged that Republicans were “routed” in the midterms after he funneled nearly half a billion dollars toward GOP candidates, especially in Texas.

“I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it,” said Musk, adding that he wished he could “rewind the clock” and put down less dough.

The Tesla and SpaceX CEO’s post-midterm switcheroo comes a little over two years after he jumped for joy onstage at a Trump rally in Pennsylvania and tipped his black MAGA hat to the crowd while declaring to be “dark MAGA.”

Upon Trump’s second inauguration, he found an early home in the administration as the chainsaw-wielding head of his so-called Department of Government Efficiency before leaving the post some months later.

After his White House exit, he publicly split with Trump over his “big, beautiful bill,” toyed with starting his own political party, and put Trump on blast by dropping a “really big bomb” on his X platform: that the president was named in the Justice Department’s files on late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Well, that post was scrubbed off the site soon after, and Musk has since — for now — seemingly found his way back in the president’s good graces.

In September, he took part in Trump’s “super intelligence” meeting with fellow tech executives at the White House and, just last month, the president presented him with a National Medal of Science.

Trump, in remarks to Musk at the medal ceremony, described the billionaire as an “industrial titan, a brilliant engineer and one of the greatest technology founders to ever live.”

“Quite honestly, there is nobody like him,” Trump said.
